correctness.rationale: For uniform normalized facet-area measure, coordinate variance is (d+2)/(3d), giving kernel 1+(3d/(d+2)) x·y. Convexity maximizes its integral absolute value at any cube vertex; sign of the kernel attains it. At a vertex the dot-product law is a pinned fair sign plus d−1 independent continuous uniform variables; exact Irwin–Hall truncation proves rational finite norms in all dimensions. Fourier expansion of the uniform-characteristic function and bounded-shift density expansion give the first correction −47/60. The volume counterpart has +13/60, so the asymptotic gap follows. Embedded checker independently passed 60 exact-rational/numerical assertions; finite checks do not establish infinite theorems.

value.rationale: Continuous normalized facet area and normalized volume are canonical but distinct sampling measures for least-squares approximation on a cube. Error amplification in the sup norm is determined exactly for facet sampling, providing an infinite rational family and a sharp high-dimensional coefficient. The d^(-1/2) leading surface-versus-volume gap distinguishes two natural geometries and cannot be read from the already known volume formula alone. This is a motivated quantitative stability problem, not an arbitrary numerical slice.
